description.narrative: Sverige bidrar till OECDs "Sector Competitiveness Strategy for Ukraine", 2009 - 2015. Huvudsektorer är jordbruksnäring, byggande av maskineri och transportredskap, förnybara energikällor och teknologi för energieffektivitet. Som ett komplement till de analytiska studierna kring jordbruksnäringen har Sida fått ett förslag att stödja utvecklingen av ett kreditgarantisystem.

Sweden is supporting the OECD "Sector Competitiveness Strategy for Ukraine", 2009 -2015. Key sectors are agribusiness, machinery and transport equipment manufacturing, renewable and energy-efficiency technologies sectors. As a complement to the above, Sida is proposed to support a Credit Guarantee Scheme for Small and Medium Enterprises in agribusiness (2013-2015).

The general outcomes are described in the section below and this section will focus more on general overarching examples and other consideration. The evaluation notes that OECDs "rigorous analytical approach and methodology" "left a lasting impression on many participants". This change in mind-set is difficult to asses in term of quantifiable outputs but is an important element in supporting long-term institutional change. In terms of expected results the more tangible results appear to be in activities related to investment, in particular in the energy sector but also agriculture. An unexpected result was the successful dialogue with the Ministry of Economy and NBU that led to the creation of the "Credit Guarantee Scheme in Ukraine" (PLANit:55070051) contribution. It must also be noted that phase III was first designed in 2013 and that the "Revolution of Dignity" caused both difficulties for project implementation but also resulted in substantial staff turnover as well as changing government priorities. As such this hugely impactful event must be taking into account when assessing the results of the contribution. In may ways it is impressive that the contribution managed to continue at all with activities and actually achieve results. One of the key motivations behind the third phase was the greater focus on implementing recommendations from phases 1 and 2, and this was substantially hampered by the political turmoil.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
